name: wallet_entries
title: Wallet Entries
description: Every movement of a wallet's balance, append-only: this ledger IS the balance (wallets.balance_minor is a rollup over it), so an entry is never edited or deleted -- a mistaken charge is corrected by a compensating entry that says so, exactly as refunds correct payments and reversing journals correct postings (docs/logic-decisions.md #3). amount_minor is signed: credits positive, debits negative, in the wallet denomination's smallest unit. generated_from carries provenance for machine-written entries (a Stripe top-up stamps its event, an auto-replenishment stamps its charge), which is what makes redelivery and re-runs safe by construction rather than by a dedup table. The reason a customer can always be shown WHY their balance is what it is: every entry names its kind, its amount, and what caused it.

fields.name: amount_minor
fields.label: Amount
fields.help: Signed: a credit is positive, a debit negative. Integer minor units, never a float.

fields.name: kind
fields.label: Kind
fields.help: topup: the customer paid. auto_topup: the saved card was charged by the threshold rule. debit: usage drawn down. refund/promo/adjustment: money back, granted, or corrected. hold: money RESERVED against a commitment that has not executed yet (negative, so the balance gate fires at the moment of commitment rather than the moment of spending -- a template run queued against 5 cents of balance must be refused before the provider is paid real money, not billed after). release: a hold handed back at settlement, always in full, always paired to its hold by generated_from marker. The actual charge for a settled commitment is an ORDINARY debit, deliberately: a released hold must never read as a refund in the reports that already exist, because a hold is not a debit that got undone -- it is money that was never spent, and the ledger should say so.

fields.name: description
fields.label: Description
fields.help: What this was for, in words the customer would accept on a statement.

fields.name: reference
fields.label: Reference
fields.help: The thing that caused it: a task id, an invoice number, a provider charge.

fields.name: generated_from
fields.label: Generated From
fields.help: Provenance for machine-written entries (stripe_evt/..., auto_topup/...). Its presence is what makes a replay a no-op instead of a second charge.
